scanNote:
GRAMMAR REFERENCE, 6-BET (121-bet). Yuqorida o'ngda 'Grammar Reference'.

CHAP USTUN (Unit 5 davomi):
'PRESENT CONTINUOUS': 'We can use the present continuous for actions we have already arranged to do in the near future. (fixed arrangements) I am flying to Madrid tomorrow.'
'CONDITIONAL 1': 'We use the first conditional to talk about real or very probable situations in the present or future.' QUTI: 'If + present simple, will + bare infinitive'. 'If you don't eat, you will be hungry. If I study hard, I'll do well in the test.'
'WHEN - IF': 'We use when to show that something will certainly happen. When Tom comes, I'll cook dinner. We use if when we are not certain that something will happen. If Tom comes, I'll cook dinner.'
To'q sariq 'UNIT 6'. 'SOME/ANY': • We use some in the affirmative with uncountable nouns or countable nouns in the plural. 'I want some milk and some biscuits.' • We also use some for offers or requests. 'Would you like some cake? (offer) Can I have some water, please? (request)' • We use any in negations and questions. 'I haven't got any strawberries. Have you got any oranges?'
'MUCH/MANY': 'We use much and many in questions and negations. Many goes before plural countable nouns. Much goes before uncountable nouns. Is there much milk in the fridge? There isn't much tea left. Have you got many friends? I haven't got many friends.'

O'NG USTUN:
'A FEW/A LITTLE': • We use a few (= not many; some) with countable nouns. 'I want a few biscuits.' • We use a little (= not much; some) with uncountable nouns. 'I want a little milk.'
'GIVING ADVICE': • We use should to say what the right/best thing to do is. 'You should take regular exercise. (= It's a good idea.)' • We use shouldn't to say what isn't the right/best thing to do. 'You shouldn't throw rubbish in the street. (= It isn't a good idea.)'
Ko'k 'UNIT 7'. 'PRESENT PERFECT'. 'Regular Verb'. KO'K JADVAL: Affirmative - Long form: I have worked, you have worked, he has worked, she has worked, it has worked, we have worked, you have worked, they have worked. Short form: I've worked, you've worked, he's worked, she's worked, it's worked, we've worked, you've worked, they've worked. Interrogative: Have I worked? Have you worked? Has he worked? Has she worked? Has it worked? Have we worked? Have you worked? Have they worked? Negative - Long form: I have not worked ... they have not worked. Short form: I haven't worked, you haven't worked, he hasn't worked, she hasn't worked, it hasn't worked, we haven't worked, you haven't worked, they haven't worked.

Bet raqami: pastda o'ngda '121'.

sections.title: Unit 5 - Present Continuous (future); Conditional 1; When - If

exercises.instructionEn: Present continuous for fixed arrangements: I am flying to Madrid tomorrow. Conditional 1: If + present simple, will + bare infinitive. If you don't eat, you will be hungry. When - If: When Tom comes, I'll cook dinner. (certain) If Tom comes, I'll cook dinner. (not certain)
exercises.instructionUz: Aniq rejalar uchun hozirgi davomli: Ertaga Madridga uchaman. 1-tur shart: If + hozirgi oddiy, will + 'to'siz infinitiv. Agar ovqatlanmasang, och qolasan. When - If: Tom kelganda kechki ovqat pishiraman. (aniq) Agar Tom kelsa, kechki ovqat pishiraman. (aniq emas)
exercises.explanationUz:
KELAJAK - UChTA USUL (5-unit):

  1 WILL - bashorat, shu zahoti
    qaror
  2 BE GOING TO - reja, dalilli
    bashorat
  3 PRESENT CONTINUOUS - ANIQ
    KELIShILGAN reja (fixed
    arrangement):
    'I AM FLYING to Madrid
     tomorrow.' (chipta olingan)


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  1-TUR ShART GAPI                ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  IF + PRESENT SIMPLE, WILL + FE'L

  REAL yoki JUDA EHTIMOLLI vaziyat
  (hozir yoki kelajakda):
  "If you DON'T EAT, you WILL BE
   hungry."
  "If I STUDY hard, I'LL DO well."

  ⚠ 'if' bo'lagida WILL YO'Q:
  'If it will rain' ✗ → 'If it
  rains' ✓


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  WHEN yoki IF?                   ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  WHEN = ANIQ bo'ladi (qachon?):
    'WHEN Tom comes, I'll cook.'
    (Tom albatta keladi)
  IF = ANIQ EMAS (agar):
    'IF Tom comes, I'll cook.'
    (kelishi noma'lum)


⚠ 'BARE INFINITIVE':

  = 'to'siz infinitiv.


⚠ 'PROBABLE':

  = ehtimolli.


⚠ 'CERTAIN':

  = aniq, ishonchli.

points.en: We can use the present continuous for actions we have already arranged to do in the near future (fixed arrangements). I am flying to Madrid tomorrow.
points.uz: Hozirgi davomli zamonni yaqin kelajakda qilishga allaqachon kelishilgan ishlar uchun ishlatishimiz mumkin (aniq rejalar). Ertaga Madridga uchaman.

points.en: We use the first conditional to talk about real or very probable situations in the present or future. If + present simple, will + bare infinitive. If you don't eat, you will be hungry. If I study hard, I'll do well in the test.
points.uz: 1-tur shart gapini hozirgi yoki kelajakdagi real yoki juda ehtimolli vaziyatlar uchun ishlatamiz. If + hozirgi oddiy, will + 'to'siz infinitiv. Agar ovqatlanmasang, och qolasan. Agar qattiq o'qisam, testda yaxshi natija ko'rsataman.

points.en: We use when to show that something will certainly happen. When Tom comes, I'll cook dinner. We use if when we are not certain that something will happen. If Tom comes, I'll cook dinner.
points.uz: 'When' ni biror narsa albatta bo'lishini ko'rsatish uchun ishlatamiz. Tom kelganda kechki ovqat pishiraman. 'If' ni biror narsa bo'lishiga ishonchimiz komil bo'lmaganda ishlatamiz. Agar Tom kelsa, kechki ovqat pishiraman.

sections.title: Unit 6 - Some/Any; Much/Many; A few/A little; Giving Advice
sections.titleUz: 6-unit - Some/Any; Much/Many; A few/A little; Maslahat berish

exercises.explanationUz:
MIQDOR SO'ZLARI.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  SOME / ANY                      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  SOME - IJOBIY gapda (sanalmaydigan
  yoki ko'plik):
    'I want SOME milk and SOME
     biscuits.'
  SOME - TAKLIF va ILTIMOSDA:
    'Would you like SOME cake?'
    (taklif)
    'Can I have SOME water?'
    (iltimos)
  ANY - INKOR va SAVOLDA:
    "I haven't got ANY strawberries."
    'Have you got ANY oranges?'


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  MUCH / MANY                     ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  Savol va inkorda:
  MANY + SANALADIGAN ko'plik:
    'Have you got MANY friends?'
    "I haven't got MANY friends."
  MUCH + SANALMAYDIGAN:
    'Is there MUCH milk?'
    "There isn't MUCH tea left."


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  A FEW / A LITTLE                ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  A FEW (= bir nechta) + SANALADIGAN:
    'I want A FEW biscuits.'
  A LITTLE (= biroz) + SANALMAYDIGAN:
    'I want A LITTLE milk.'


⚠ SANALADIGAN / SANALMAYDIGAN:

  SANALADIGAN: biscuits, oranges,
  friends (ko'plik bor)
  SANALMAYDIGAN: milk, water, tea
  (ko'plik yo'q)


⚠ 'AN OFFER':

  = taklif.


⚠ 'A REQUEST':

  = iltimos.
exercises.bookRef: Coursebook, 121-bet, Some/Any, Much/Many, A few/A little

points.en: We use some in the affirmative with uncountable nouns or countable nouns in the plural. I want some milk and some biscuits. We also use some for offers or requests. Would you like some cake? Can I have some water, please?
points.uz: 'Some' ni tasdiqda sanalmaydigan otlar yoki ko'plik sanaladigan otlar bilan ishlatamiz. Men biroz sut va biroz pechenye xohlayman. 'Some' ni taklif yoki iltimoslarda ham ishlatamiz. Tort xohlaysizmi? Biroz suv olsam bo'ladimi?

points.en: We use any in negations and questions. I haven't got any strawberries. Have you got any oranges?
points.uz: 'Any' ni inkor va savollarda ishlatamiz. Menda qulupnay yo'q. Sizda apelsin bormi?

points.en: We use much and many in questions and negations. Many goes before plural countable nouns. Much goes before uncountable nouns. Is there much milk in the fridge? There isn't much tea left. Have you got many friends? I haven't got many friends.
points.uz: 'Much' va 'many' ni savol va inkorlarda ishlatamiz. 'Many' ko'plik sanaladigan otlardan oldin. 'Much' sanalmaydigan otlardan oldin. Muzlatgichda ko'p sut bormi? Ko'p choy qolmagan. Do'stlaringiz ko'pmi? Do'stlarim ko'p emas.

points.en: We use a few (= not many; some) with countable nouns. I want a few biscuits. We use a little (= not much; some) with uncountable nouns. I want a little milk.
points.uz: 'A few' (= ko'p emas; bir nechta) ni sanaladigan otlar bilan ishlatamiz. Bir nechta pechenye xohlayman. 'A little' (= ko'p emas; biroz) ni sanalmaydigan otlar bilan ishlatamiz. Biroz sut xohlayman.
points.noteUz: ⚠ a few - sanaladigan; a little - sanalmaydigan.

exercises.instructionEn: Giving advice. We use should to say what the right/best thing to do is. You should take regular exercise. We use shouldn't to say what isn't the right/best thing to do. You shouldn't throw rubbish in the street.
exercises.instructionUz: Maslahat berish. 'Should' ni to'g'ri/eng yaxshi ish nima ekanini aytish uchun ishlatamiz. Muntazam jismoniy mashq qilishingiz kerak. 'Shouldn't' ni to'g'ri/eng yaxshi ish emasligini aytish uchun ishlatamiz. Ko'chaga axlat tashlamasligingiz kerak.
exercises.explanationUz:
MASLAHAT - SHOULD.

  SHOULD + FE'L = ... kerak (yaxshi
  fikr)
    'You SHOULD take regular
     exercise.' (= It's a good idea.)
  SHOULDN'T + FE'L = ...masligi
    kerak (yomon fikr)
    "You SHOULDN'T throw rubbish in
     the street." (= It isn't a good
     idea.)

  ⚠ 'should' dan keyin 'to' YO'Q.
  ⚠ 'should' hamma shaxsda bir xil
  ('he should', 'he shoulds' ✗).


⚠ 'REGULAR EXERCISE':

  = muntazam jismoniy mashq.


⚠ 'TO THROW RUBBISH':

  = axlat tashlamoq.

points.en: We use should to say what the right/best thing to do is. You should take regular exercise. (= It's a good idea.)
points.uz: 'Should' ni to'g'ri/eng yaxshi ish nima ekanini aytish uchun ishlatamiz. Muntazam jismoniy mashq qilishingiz kerak. (= Bu yaxshi fikr.)

points.en: We use shouldn't to say what isn't the right/best thing to do. You shouldn't throw rubbish in the street. (= It isn't a good idea.)
points.uz: 'Shouldn't' ni to'g'ri/eng yaxshi ish emasligini aytish uchun ishlatamiz. Ko'chaga axlat tashlamasligingiz kerak. (= Bu yaxshi fikr emas.)

exercises.instructionEn: Present Perfect - Regular Verb. Affirmative: I have (I've) worked, he has (he's) worked. Interrogative: Have I worked? Has he worked? Negative: I have not (haven't) worked, he has not (hasn't) worked.
exercises.instructionUz: Hozirgi tugallangan zamon - to'g'ri fe'l. Tasdiq: I have (I've) worked, he has (he's) worked. So'roq: Have I worked? Has he worked? Inkor: I have not (haven't) worked, he has not (hasn't) worked.
exercises.explanationUz:
PRESENT PERFECT - ShAKLI.

  HAVE / HAS + FE'LNING 3-ShAKLI
  (past participle)

  To'g'ri fe'llar: -ED (worked)
  Noto'g'ri fe'llar: 3-shakl (seen,
  gone, done - ro'yxat 128-betda)


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  TASDIQ                          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  I / you / we / they HAVE worked
    = I've / you've / we've /
      they've worked
  he / she / it HAS worked
    = he's / she's / it's worked

  ⚠ "he's" = he HAS (bu yerda), he
  IS emas! Kontekstga qarang:
  "he's worked" (has), "he's
  working" (is).


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  SO'ROQ                          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  HAVE I / you / we / they worked?
  HAS he / she / it worked?


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  INKOR                           ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  I HAVEN'T worked (have not)
  he HASN'T worked (has not)


⚠ IShLATILIShI - keyingi betda.

points.en: Affirmative: I have worked (I've worked), you have worked, he has worked (he's worked), she has worked, it has worked, we have worked, they have worked.
points.uz: Tasdiq: I have worked (I've worked), you have worked, he has worked (he's worked), she has worked, it has worked, we have worked, they have worked.

points.en: Interrogative: Have I worked? Have you worked? Has he worked? Has she worked? Has it worked? Have we worked? Have they worked?
points.uz: So'roq: Have I worked? Have you worked? Has he worked? Has she worked? Has it worked? Have we worked? Have they worked?

points.en: Negative: I have not worked (I haven't worked), he has not worked (he hasn't worked), they have not worked (they haven't worked).
points.uz: Inkor: I have not worked (I haven't worked), he has not worked (he hasn't worked), they have not worked (they haven't worked).
